Las Vegas Holiday Invitational champions |bowl= [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], First Round |bowl_result= }} {{2018–19 Mountain West Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2018–19 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Nevada, Reno]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wolf Pack, led by fourth-year head coach [[Eric Musselman]], played their home games at the [[Lawlor Events Center]] on their campus in [[Reno, Nevada]] as members of the [[Mountain West Conference]] (MW). They finished the season 29–5, 15–3 in Mountain West play to share the regular season Mountain West championship with [[2018–19 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team|Utah State]]. They defeated [[2018–19 Boise State Broncos men's basketball team|Boise State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2019 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|Mountain West tournament]] before losing in the semifinals to [[2018–19 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2018–19 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. On April 7, head coach Eric Musselman resigned to become the head coach at [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26462667/arkansas-hires-nevada-musselman-coach|title = Arkansas hires Nevada's Musselman as coach|date = 7 April 2019}} He finished at Nevada with a four-year record of 110–34, three trips to the NCAA Tournament, and were champions of the [[2016 College Basketball Invitational]]. On April 11, Nevada hired [[Steve Alford]] as their next head coach.{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26501450/ex-ucla-coach-alford-hired-lead-nevada|title=Ex-UCLA coach Alford hired to lead Nevada|date=12 April 2019}} ==Previous season== The [[2017–18 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Wolf Pack]] finished the season 29–8 overall and 15–3 in conference play to win the MW regular season championship. They defeated [[2017–18 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team|UNLV]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 Mountain West Conference men's basketball tournament|MW tournament]] before losing in the semifinals to [[2017–18 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2017-18 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] and [[2017–18 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen where they lost to [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola–Chicago]]. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" ! The team returns three players who earned all-conference recognition [[2017–18 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|last season]]—first-team members [[Jordan Caroline]] and [[Caleb Martin (basketball)|Caleb Martin]] and second-team member [[Cody Martin (basketball)|Cody Martin]], with Caleb Martin also having been named Player of the Year by MW coaches.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2018/3/6/mountain-west-announces-2017-18-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx |title=Mountain West Announces 2017-18 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 6, 2018 |accessdate=October 20, 2018}}{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2018/3/19/mountain-west-mens-basketball-all-conference-media-awards.aspx |title=Mountain West Men's Basketball All-Conference Media Awards |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 4, 2018 |accessdate=October 20, 2018}} Additionally, six transfers who averaged at least 13 points per game in their immediately previous seasons of college play will become eligible this season.{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/24992844/college-basketball-preseason-power-rankings |title=KU, UK top college basketball preseason power rankings |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=October 19, 2018 |accessdate=October 20, 2018}} At the conference's media days in [[Las Vegas]], Caroline and the Martin twins were named as preseason first-team all-conference picks for 2018–19, with Caleb Martin picked as the preseason Player of the Year. [[Jordan Brown (basketball)|Jordan Brown]], who headed the Pack's 2018 recruiting class, was named preseason Freshman of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2018/10/15/2018-19-mountain-west-mens-basketball-preseason-all-conference-team.aspx |title=2018-19 Mountain West Men's Basketball Preseason All-Conference Team |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=October 16, 2018 |accessdate=October 20, 2018}} The Pack were also the overwhelming choice for the MW regular-season title, receiving all but one of the possible first-place votes.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2018/10/15/nevada-predicted-to-win-the-2018-19-mountain-west-mens-basketball-regular-season-title.aspx |title=Nevada Predicted to Win the 2018-19 Mountain West Men's Basketball Regular-Season Title |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=October 16, 2018 |accessdate=October 20, 2018}} ==Roster== {{CBB roster/Header|year=2018|team=Nevada Wolf Pack|teamcolors=y|high_school=yes}} {{CBB roster/Player |first=Tre'Shawn |last=Thurman |link=y |num=0 |pos=F |ft=6 |in=7 |lbs=230 |class=sr |rs=y |home=[[Omaha, Nebraska|Omaha, NE]] |high_school=[[Omaha Central High School|Omaha Central HS]]
